the Ordovician succession along the western shore in the Hinlopen Strait is a classic example of an eustatic-controlled, carbonate-dominated shelf succession, which is characterized by a high degree of shallowing and deepening cycles and by the presence of numerous, mostly peritidal dolomite facies.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the succession is characterized by a very high sedimentation rate of 2 mm/yr and that it represents an inner platform setting, which is very similar to that of the Laurentian platform, but which is located in the middle of the Iapetus Ocean.

the Kirtonrygen and Valhall Fonna formations, and the entire Sauk IIIB supersequence, were deposited in the inner part of a shallow marine carbonate platform, with a very shallow-water, low-energy, peritidal depositional environment in the early part of the succession and a more shallow-water, high-energy, periplatform environment during the late part of the succession.

the succession is a typical example of an Ordovician peritidal platform with a long-term, highstand to lowstand transition, which is characterized by the development of the so-called “Sauk IIIB-type” platform margin.
